source.title: Balanced Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Imbalanced Regression
source.authors: Ya-Hao Liu; Qin Wang; Li-Xin Duan; Wen Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. No document or truncation problem is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates sharpness-aware training and sharpness measures in imbalanced vision regression, a new setting. Its results do not test any listed version’s specific claim about same-distribution generalization, magnitude-aware sharpness, or the other named conditions.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-set regression errors and loss-landscape measurements for imbalanced regression. These bear on generalization and sharpness in a related setting, but it does not report train-versus-test error gaps or test any listed version as stated. Its results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to develop BSAM and evaluates imbalanced regression performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware training sharpness, train–test gaps, or ranking against other generalization measures. Figure 1 measures test-loss landscapes across sample subsets; Table 8 reports Hessian curvature. None of the other versions is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: targeted reweighting during perturbation computation improves overall imbalanced regression performance across three benchmarks while retaining standard SAM's computational efficiency. Their claim of balancing generalization across the distribution is an interpretation, not a demonstrated improvement in every region and metric: for example, NYUD2-DIR many- and medium-shot RMSE worsen relative to SQINV.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a modified sharpness-aware optimization method for imbalanced regression; it does not reproduce any of the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and target-density subset affect the reported performance and sharpness measurements; the study also compares SAM variants and reweighting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports higher MAE and a sharper test-loss landscape for low-density AgeDB-DIR samples: 10.68 versus 6.67 overall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-density target regions can have higher test error and greater test-loss sensitivity to parameter perturbations than the overall evaluation set.

fits_no_version.finding: For AgeDB-DIR few-shot samples, BSAM reduces the reported maximum Hessian eigenvalue from 141.21 to 86.51 and trace from 653.53 to 90.88 relative to SQINV.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BSAM produces lower reported Hessian curvature than SQINV in this imbalanced regression setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Overall AgeDB-DIR test MAE is 6.391 for SQINV, 6.230 with SAM, 6.184 with ImbSAM, and 6.067 with BSAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These sharpness-aware training variants improve overall AgeDB-DIR test MAE over SQINV under the tested recipe.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says “The code is available here” but supplies no URL)
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: Reported comparisons generally provide no uncertainty estimates. The loss-landscape comparison uses different sample subsets and does not measure a train-test error gap. Table 8 averages over three experiments but reports no variability.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant results were omitted. Other tables report regression-method comparisons or additional metrics, but do not measure a listed version or a distinct result needed to characterize the related sharpness/generalization findings.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance performance with random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, training-set size dependence, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware training sharpness versus train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T3/tests classification conflicts with its correct identification that no listed version is measured. Section 3.1 discusses distribution-shift limitations of a SAM bound, but does not establish a counterexample to V7's empirical correlation. States are assessed against the listed versions; cannot_determine does not dispute the reported numerical improvements.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: regression model
rows.operation_detail: Compares loss landscape and MAE for the entire AgeDB-DIR dataset with samples from low-density regions.
rows.note: The caption identifies the whole-dataset view as the left panel.
rows.check: Figure 1 visualizes test-observation loss, not training sharpness or a train–test gap. The caption supports MAE 6.67; the model and perturbation normalization are unspecified.

rows.subject: regression model
rows.operation_detail: Measures loss landscape and MAE for low-density samples under controlled parameter perturbation.
rows.value: MAE 10.68; significantly increased sharpness and sensitivity to parameter perturbations
rows.note: Comparison is across different sample subsets, not a reported train-test error gap.
rows.check: MAE 10.68 and increased test-loss sharpness compare low-density samples with the overall test set. This does not measure V7's relationship across trained networks.

rows.subject: SQINV
rows.operation_detail: Reports maximum Hessian eigenvalue and Hessian trace for the few-shot scenario.
rows.measure: maximum Hessian eigenvalue λmax and Hessian trace Tr(H)
rows.note: These curvature measures are not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or a measured train-test gap.
rows.check: Values match Table 8, but SQINV denotes a training method. Hessian eigenvalue and trace do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or a train–test gap.

rows.subject: BSAM
rows.operation_detail: Reports maximum Hessian eigenvalue and Hessian trace for the few-shot scenario.
rows.measure: maximum Hessian eigenvalue λmax and Hessian trace Tr(H)
rows.note: The authors say lower values indicate smoother, flatter landscapes associated with better generalization.
rows.check: Values match Table 8, but BSAM denotes a training method. Lower Hessian curvature alone cannot establish V7; the reported comparison lacks train–test gaps and magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: SQINV
rows.operation_detail: Trains with square-root-inverse weighting on the AgeDB-DIR benchmark; reports test MAE by density region.
rows.note: Imbalanced-regression test performance; no train error or train-test gap is reported.
rows.check: The value matches Table 6. This is a method-performance baseline, not evidence for any listed version.

rows.subject: + SAM
rows.operation_detail: Applies standard SAM to the SQINV baseline; reports test MAE by density region.
rows.note: The table reports the overall MAE for standard SAM.
rows.check: The value and baseline match Table 6. Improved test MAE under SAM does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: + imbSAM

rows.note: The table reports the overall MAE for ImbSAM.
rows.check: The value and baseline match Table 6. Improved test MAE under ImbSAM does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: + BSAM
